comments.body:
RECOMMENDATION (analysis only — NOT implemented; this needs a human decision on AC1, and one of the two options is a security-posture change).

## Findings

1. **0707 is the ONLY bedrock-pinned module in the llm_live matrix lane.** The other bedrock-pinned file, tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py, carries NO `_live_llm_ready` sentinel — it is plain `pytest.mark.external` with its own `REBAR_LIVE_BEDROCK=1` opt-in, so it runs in the complement (`external`) job and skips there unless explicitly enabled. It is unaffected.

2. **The precise defect is a disagreement inside 0707, not in the workflow.** The module sets `_live_llm_ready = _live_llm.live_llm_ready()`, and that probe answers 'is the credential present for the provider THIS ARM RESOLVES from the standard model class'. But the module then bypasses model-class resolution entirely and pins `_MODEL = "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"`. On the anthropic arm the probe says READY (an Anthropic key exists) while every cell actually calls Bedrock. A module's readiness sentinel must agree with the model it pins; here it cannot.

3. **Cost dimension:** the module is 2 tests, one of which runs `_TRIALS = 3`. Running it on all three arms triples those billable calls to assert the same thing about the same model.

## Recommended: AC1 option (a), implemented as a provider-aware sentinel

Make 0707's readiness reflect the provider it PINS (bedrock) rather than the arm's configured provider, so it executes on the bedrock arm and skips on anthropic/openai.

- No security-posture change: the OIDC step stays gated to `matrix.provider == 'bedrock'`.
- Honest coverage: the anthropic arm never claimed to cover Bedrock; skipping is accurate, and the arm still FAILS loudly if its OWN credential is missing (the preflight is untouched).
- Canary-safe: the all-skip canary fires only when collected>=1 and executed==0. Other llm_live tests still execute on non-bedrock arms, so it stays green-for-the-right-reason.
- Has in-repo precedent: test_bedrock_cache_live.py already self-gates on a bedrock-specific opt-in.
- Cheaper: removes duplicate live calls on two arms.

## Against option (b) — un-gating the OIDC step to all arms

This hands AWS credentials to jobs that do not need them, including the arms that hold third-party API keys (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY), widening the blast radius of the scoped Bedrock CI role for ZERO coverage gain — it would call the same model from three arms and learn the same fact three times. Recommend rejecting unless someone wants bedrock-pinned modules to run everywhere for an independent reason. It is also a change an agent should not make unilaterally.

## Third option worth an explicit rejection

Un-pinning `_MODEL` so the eval follows each arm would turn a single-model regression reproduction into a cross-provider behavioral eval. That is a different test with a different purpose (and 3x the spend); the pin exists to hold the model fixed while reproducing bug 0707. Recommend keeping the pin.

## Regardless of the choice

Consider a guard test asserting that any module carrying `_live_llm_ready` does not hard-pin a provider prefix that contradicts its readiness probe — that invariant is what failed here, and it will fail again the next time someone pins a model in this tier.

Note on the already-landing region fix (Gerrit 1658, ticket 79d6): it stays correct under every option above. Exporting a region on all arms is harmless where unused and is required the moment any module pins bedrock.

comments.body:
DISPOSITION RECORDED (per coordinator direction) — do not re-litigate:

**Option (b), un-gating the OIDC credential step to all arms: REJECTED.** It hands AWS credentials to arms holding third-party API keys (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY), widening the blast radius of the scoped Bedrock CI role, for zero coverage gain — the same model called from three arms teaches the same fact three times. The OIDC step stays gated `if: matrix.provider == 'bedrock'`.

**Also rejected: un-pinning _MODEL** so the eval follows each arm. The pin exists to hold the model fixed while reproducing bug 0707; unpinning converts a single-model regression reproduction into a 3x-spend cross-provider eval — a different test with a different purpose.

**Implemented: option (a), the provider-aware readiness sentinel.** Test-harness correctness only; zero credential-surface change.

Implementation notes:
- `tests/external/_live_llm.py`: `live_llm_ready()` gains an optional `required_provider`. When supplied, readiness requires the arm's `configured_provider()` to MATCH it as well as that provider's credential being present. New `skip_unless_provider(provider)` mark factory. Purely additive — the no-arg call and the module-level `skip_without_live_llm` are untouched, so the seven modules that follow the arm keep their exact behaviour.
- `tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py`: derives `_PINNED_PROVIDER` from `_MODEL` itself (so the pin and the gate cannot drift) and applies the pinned gate to both tests.
- Rendered skip on a mismatched arm: `no live LLM: this module pins a 'bedrock' model, but the configured arm resolves 'openai' — that arm cannot cover it, so it runs on the 'bedrock' arm instead`. Visible, not silent.
- Canary-safe: the all-skip canary fires only when collected>=1 and executed==0; the arm-following modules still execute on non-bedrock arms.

Incidental finding while building the structural guard: a naive substring scan for a pinned `<provider>:` model flags `test_pydantic_ai_cutover_live.py`, which merely DISCUSSES `anthropic:claude-opus-4-8` in its module docstring. The guard was tightened to match assignments only, so prose does not read as a pin. That module pins nothing and is unchanged.

compiled_state.description:
# Context

Discovered while fixing 79d6 (financial-maroon-toucan, Gerrit 1658), which unguarded the
region env so every live-LLM matrix arm resolves a Bedrock region.

`tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py` sets
`_live_llm_ready = _live_llm.live_llm_ready()` — a probe that answers "is the credential
present for the provider THIS ARM resolves from the standard model class". But the module
bypasses model-class resolution and pins `_MODEL = "bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6"`.
On the anthropic and openai arms the probe says READY (an Anthropic/OpenAI key exists) while
every cell actually calls Bedrock — an arm that carries no AWS credential, because the OIDC
step is gated `if: matrix.provider == 'bedrock'`.

A module's readiness sentinel must agree with the model it pins. Here it cannot.

It is the ONLY bedrock-pinned module in the `llm_live` lane: `test_bedrock_cache_live.py` is
also bedrock-pinned but carries no `_live_llm_ready` sentinel (plain `external` + its own
`REBAR_LIVE_BEDROCK` opt-in), so it runs in the complement job and is unaffected.

# Disposition — option (b) is REJECTED; do not re-litigate

**Un-gating the OIDC step to all arms is rejected**: it hands AWS credentials to arms holding
third-party API keys (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`), widening the blast radius of the
scoped Bedrock CI role for ZERO coverage gain — it would call the same model from three arms
and learn the same fact three times. The OIDC step stays gated to `matrix.provider == 'bedrock'`.

Also rejected: un-pinning `_MODEL` so the eval follows each arm. The pin exists to hold the
model fixed while reproducing bug 0707; unpinning turns a single-model regression reproduction
into a 3x-spend cross-provider eval, which is a different test with a different purpose.

**Approved: option (a) — a provider-aware readiness sentinel.** Test-harness correctness with
zero credential-surface change.

# Plan

1. `tests/external/_live_llm.py`: give `live_llm_ready()` an optional `required_provider`
   argument. When supplied, readiness additionally requires the arm's `configured_provider()`
   to MATCH it, so a module that pins a provider is ready only on the arm that runs it.
   Add a `skip_unless_provider(provider)` mark factory whose reason names the mismatch
   (module pins X, arm resolves Y) so the skip is VISIBLE, not silent. Purely additive:
   the no-argument call and the module-level `skip_without_live_llm` are unchanged, so the
   seven modules that do not pin a provider keep their exact current behaviour.
2. `tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py`: pass the pinned provider to the
   sentinel and apply `skip_unless_provider("bedrock")` on both tests.
3. Regression test for the invariant.

Canary-safe: the all-skip canary fires only when collected>=1 and executed==0. On a non-bedrock
arm the other `llm_live` modules still execute, so the arm stays green for the right reason.

# Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A module that pins a provider is `_live_llm_ready` only on the arm that resolves
  that provider; on other arms it skips with a reason naming both the pinned provider and the
  arm's resolved provider.
- [ ] AC2 — `tests/external/test_completion_banking_behavior_0707.py` uses that gate for
  `bedrock`, and modules that pin nothing are behaviourally unchanged.
- [ ] AC3 — A test pins the invariant (a pinned-provider module is not ready on a mismatched
  arm, and is ready on the matching arm when its credential is present), and the rejection of
  option (b) is recorded on this ticket.
